brief: Asia saw a fading semis rebound (TSMC +4.6%, MediaTek +9.8%) aided by Taiwan's tighter short-selling rules and a NT$500bn stabilization fund; weekend Nvidia/Jensen Huang headlines look idiosyncratic but could hit sentiment, with CoreWeave and Nebius earnings this week mattering more. Positioning: last week saw the largest cut in US long/short TMT gross exposure since Covid and the biggest net cut since Liberation Day. The post-midterm 'blue tsunami' rally reversed within 24 hours because the market could not stay bearish on AI spending while bullish on the broader economy; SPX broke its range, gamma support vanished, and CTA selling accelerated alongside record put volume (>11mm puts in a day, the largest ever). Models see another ~$25bn+ of SPX CTA supply this week. Oil is lower absent weekend escalation, but the author expects the escalation premium to return by Wed/Thu absent diplomatic progress. Ukraine ceasefire odds are just 10-15%; the author's base case is a prolonged conflict, with European defense derating seen as overdone given NATO spending commitments. On AI, the medium-term risk is reframed from power/permitting constraints to oversupply, since efficiency gains could outpace demand. Semis look oversold; the author favors moving up the quality curve (ASML, TSMC) with CPI the near-term catalyst, seeing range-bound trading as the best outcome.
